dedupe_keys.name: foen biodiversity geodata and federal biotope inventories floodplains mires wildlife corridors switzerland

description: The Swiss Federal Office for the Environment publishes its biodiversity geodata on one page, grouped as federal inventories, protected areas, fauna, flora and habitats, each with its data date. The federal inventories include floodplains of national importance (2022), amphibian spawning sites, water and migratory bird reserves, raised bogs, fens and mire landscapes, dry meadows and pastures and federal hunting reserves, plus alpine floodplains and floodplains outside the inventory; protected areas include the Ramsar and Emerald sites; and fauna and habitat layers include the national ecological network (REN), supra-regional wildlife corridors (2025), river sections with high species diversity, a floodplain vegetation map and potential maps of invasive species, several as ZIP downloads. The floodplain inventory on opendata.swiss explains that the Federal Council brought it into force in 1992 with 169 objects under the Nature and Cultural Heritage Act and revised it in 2001, 2003, 2007 and 2017. Access is free, under the opendata.swiss terms of use for the datasets published there. Caveats: the page is in German, French or Italian, and some layers are given only by agreement with the FOEN biodiversity division. Coverage is Switzerland. It supports climate adaptation and hazard exposure analysis, such as locating floodplains that store floodwater near roads and rail and wildlife corridors crossed by transport lines; the related record is the Engadin protection forest case study.
